meta.title: FirstGear Question Bank
meta.note: Answers are grounded in the FirstGear Knowledge Base. Questions citing [Illustrative – Team 8] content test prototype sample content, not real PVNA facts.

questions.question: In which year was the company (then Padmini Engineering) founded?
questions.explanation: Founded in 1991 in New Delhi; Padmini VNA Mechatronics came into existence in 2005.

questions.question: What is the probation period for a new employee?
questions.explanation: Probation is 6 months with a formal assessment; it can be extended only once, by 3 months.

questions.question: Which gift to a customer is acceptable under the Code of Conduct?

options.A: A box of sweets of nominal value at Diwali, not linked to any business decision
options.B: A cash voucher for the buyer
options.C: An expensive gadget just before a nomination decision
options.D: A high-value gift card, as long as it is not cash

questions.explanation: Gifts must be nominal, never cash, lawful under the customer's policies, and never given to win or retain business.

questions.question: At an industry event, a competitor's sales head suggests you both 'keep prices steady' for a common OEM. What should you do?

options.A: Agree informally, since nothing is written down
options.B: Share only your price range, not exact numbers
options.C: Discuss it only if the OEM is not present
options.D: Decline – discussing prices or terms with competitors is prohibited collusion – and report it

questions.explanation: Communications with competitors must avoid prices, terms, customers and suppliers; collusion is illegal.

questions.question: Where can you report a Code of Conduct violation, with protection from retaliation?

options.B: To your manager, skip-level manager, HR or ethics@padminivna.com

questions.explanation: PVNA protects anyone reporting in good faith via manager, skip-level, HR or the ethics email.

questions.question: Which of these is listed under PVNA's EV category?
questions.explanation: IPM Motor, IPM Edrive, MCU/VCU, DC-DC Converter and eWP are EV products.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) system?

options.B: Lower combustion temperature and NOx emissions by recirculating exhaust

questions.explanation: EGR routes exhaust back to the intake to cut NOx – central to BS-VI compliance.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of PVNA's four vehicle segments?
questions.explanation: The four segments are 2W/3W, M&HCV and LCV, Passenger Vehicles, and Tractor & Off-Road.

questions.question: The Fuel Tank Isolation Valve belongs to which category?
questions.explanation: It is listed under Hybrid – hybrids need sealed tanks because the engine runs less often.

questions.question: A customer asks you for the lead time of a new product during a call. What should you do?

options.B: Confirm with Product/Engineering and follow the RFQ process

questions.explanation: Never quote specifications, prices or lead times from memory.

questions.question: A customer reports a defect. Which three details should you ask for first?

options.A: Part number, lot/batch number and date code
options.B: Invoice value, PO number and buyer name
options.D: Plant name, shift and operator name

questions.explanation: These enable traceability to identify, contain and clean-point the suspect lot.

questions.question: What does OTIF stand for?
questions.explanation: Delivery performance is tracked as On Time In Full.

questions.question: Can you take photos of customer parts during the plant walk?

options.B: Yes, if you don't post them online

questions.explanation: Customer parts and processes are confidential.

questions.question: What is the purpose of end-of-line (EOL) testing?

options.C: 100% functional testing (e.g. leak, flow, electrical) before packing

questions.explanation: EOL testing is where most quality issues are caught before shipment.

questions.question: In a complaint, what is the 'clean point'?

options.A: The first good lot shipped after the fix
options.B: The cleanest area of the plant
options.C: The date the complaint was closed

questions.explanation: Traceability lets PVNA tell the customer exactly from which lot parts are OK.

questions.question: What does a PPAP prove to the customer?

options.B: That the production process can consistently make parts meeting all requirements
options.D: That the supplier is financially sound

questions.explanation: PPAP must be approved before regular supply (SOP).

questions.question: Which PPAP submission level is the usual default?
questions.explanation: Level 3 is full submission with samples.

questions.question: What is the typical target for containment after a customer complaint?
questions.explanation: Contain within 24 hours: block suspect stock and sort at the customer if needed.

questions.question: PVNA wants to switch to a cheaper sub-supplier for a customer's part. What is required?

options.B: Inform the customer after the change
options.C: Notify the customer and get approval before implementing, usually with re-PPAP

questions.explanation: Unapproved changes are among the most serious quality violations.

questions.question: During a complaint call, the customer demands compensation. What should the KAM do?

options.A: Accept it to protect the relationship
options.D: Not commit; involve Quality and the Reporting Boss as per the approval matrix

questions.explanation: A KAM never admits liability or agrees compensation on their own.

questions.question: A customer asks for a tooling cost breakdown. Who is the primary owner?
questions.explanation: Costing owns piece price and tooling cost estimates.

questions.question: A journalist calls you about a new EV product. What do you do?

options.B: Decline to comment and hang up
options.C: Direct them politely to Corporate Communications and alert them

questions.explanation: Only authorised spokespersons speak to the media.

questions.question: A customer changes next week's delivery schedule. Who must you inform?
questions.explanation: Schedule changes go immediately to Planning/SCM.

questions.question: Which system holds HR policies, leave and reimbursements?
questions.explanation: Employee login on the website points to Pconnect on Darwinbox.

questions.question: What is the routing rule of thumb when a customer asks a question you can't answer?

options.B: Tell them when you'll respond, not what the answer is, until the owner confirms
options.C: Ask the customer to call Engineering directly
options.D: Wait until the next monthly review

questions.explanation: Route to the owner, commit to a response time, escalate if missed.

questions.question: Who approves a price 5% below target margin?
questions.explanation: 3–7% below target margin needs Business Head / CFO approval.

questions.question: What can a new KAM do on their own during Days 1–30?
questions.explanation: New KAMs make no pricing, delivery or compensation commitments.

questions.question: A customer's assembly line may stop tomorrow because of our parts. What escalation level is this?
questions.explanation: Line-stop risk is L3: Business Head plus Head of Quality/Plant, same day.

questions.question: Who approves a change in a customer's payment terms?
questions.explanation: Payment terms affect working capital; CFO approval is required.

questions.question: Which of these is a KAM KPI?
questions.explanation: KPIs include RFQ turnaround, conversion, bookings, complaint response, collections and CSAT.

questions.question: What is the first thing a KAM does on receiving an RFQ?

options.A: Acknowledge it the same day and log it in CRM

questions.explanation: Step 1: receive, log in CRM, acknowledge the customer.

questions.question: The RFQ drawing is Rev B but the specification refers to Rev C. What do you do?

options.C: Quote both and let the customer choose
options.D: Raise a clarification immediately; never quote on an unclear revision

questions.explanation: Quoting on the wrong revision is a common and costly mistake.

questions.question: Who owns technical feasibility in the RFQ process?
questions.explanation: Engineering/NPD provides the feasibility commitment and deviations list.

questions.question: The customer asks for 'just a ballpark price' before internal approval. What do you say?

options.C: Politely decline and commit to a date for the approved quotation
options.D: Ask the competitor what they quoted

questions.explanation: Never share any price before internal approval.

questions.question: Who makes the Go / No-Go decision on an RFQ?
questions.explanation: Based on strategic fit, capacity, capability and margin potential.

questions.question: What does tooling amortisation mean?

options.A: The customer pays for tooling upfront
options.C: Tooling cost is spread into the piece price over an agreed volume

questions.explanation: The alternative is customer-paid (customer-owned) tooling.

questions.question: What is raw-material indexation?

options.A: Periodic price adjustment based on published commodity indices

questions.explanation: Common in OEM contracts, e.g. quarterly for steel, aluminium, copper.

questions.question: What do Incoterms decide?

options.B: Who pays freight and who carries risk in transit

questions.explanation: E.g. Ex-Works, FCA, DAP.

questions.question: In a negotiation, the customer pushes for a price below your agreed mandate. What should you do?

options.C: Offer an extra discount on another part
options.D: Say you will confirm after internal review; don't exceed your mandate

questions.explanation: Agree the mandate with the KAM Head before the meeting and never exceed it.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of the piece-price build-up?
questions.explanation: Piece price = material + bought-out + conversion + overheads + packaging/logistics + provisions + SG&A + margin.

questions.question: What is the correct order of these programme milestones?

options.B: Nomination → Design freeze → PPAP approval → SOP

questions.explanation: Nomination, kick-off, design freeze, tooling, samples, PPAP, pilot, SOP.

questions.question: In the 8D method, what is D3?
questions.explanation: D3 = sort, block, replace to protect the customer immediately.

questions.question: D4 root cause analysis must address which two questions?

options.A: Why it occurred and why it escaped detection
options.B: Who caused it and how much it cost

questions.explanation: Occurrence and escape root causes, using 5-Why and fishbone.

questions.question: What is the KAM's role in an 8D?

options.C: Ensure timely containment, review the 8D before it goes out, and keep the customer updated

questions.explanation: The KAM must not speculate on root cause before Quality confirms.

questions.question: Why must engineering changes during a programme be priced?
questions.explanation: Every change is assessed for cost, timing and validation and formally agreed.

questions.question: A buyer says your quote is 8% above a competitor and asks you to match it today. Best response?

options.A: Match it to win the business
options.B: Clarify like-for-like scope, explain value, and commit to a response date after internal review
options.D: Ask for the competitor's quote document

questions.explanation: An 8% cut is beyond KAM authority; never ask for a competitor's confidential quote.

questions.question: A customer buyer hints that an expensive festival gift would help the nomination. What do you do?

options.B: Ask your manager to send it instead
options.C: Politely decline, inform your manager, and report via ethics email if pressure continues

questions.explanation: Gifts must never be given to win business.

questions.question: At 7:30 pm a customer reports 40 failing parts and a possible line stop. Which is correct?

options.A: Wait until morning to inform Quality
options.B: Gather traceability data, escalate as L3 to Quality/Plant and KAM Head the same evening, and ensure containment within 24 hours
options.D: Tell the customer it is their assembly problem

questions.explanation: Line-stop risk is an L3 escalation; no liability or compensation commitments.

questions.question: Who approves a price below the floor price?
questions.explanation: More than 7% below target margin or below floor needs CEO approval.

questions.question: Using a competitor's leaked price list to prepare your quote is:

options.A: Acceptable if it came from the customer
options.B: Prohibited – it breaches the Code of Conduct on industrial espionage and fair competition

questions.explanation: Don't appropriate or use anyone's confidential information.

questions.question: Since when has Aravalli Motors (fictional demo account) been a PVNA customer?
questions.explanation: First nomination was a canister purge valve in 2012.

questions.question: What is the current delivery issue on the Aravalli account?

options.C: OTIF at 93% due to a sub-supplier PCB shortage

questions.explanation: Target OTIF is 98%; a recovery plan with SCM is in place.

questions.question: Which Aravalli part is PPAP-approved with SOP next quarter?
questions.explanation: eWP is in ramp-up; Charge Port Actuator starts next quarter.

questions.question: Which is the largest pipeline opportunity at Aravalli?
questions.explanation: Estimated ₹60 crore annual value; next step is a tech day.

questions.question: What should the one-page account brief contain?

options.A: Customer strategy, what we supply, account health, top 3 opportunities and risks, and a 90-day plan

questions.explanation: The mentor reviews it before Day 15.

questions.question: Who owns raw-material indexation approvals at Aravalli?
questions.explanation: She also owns powertrain RFQs.

questions.question: How should you build the relationship with Aravalli's new Head of Purchase?

options.B: By avoiding him until the next QBR
options.C: With data – supplier scorecard, cost-down ideas, localisation proposals
options.D: By offering an immediate price cut

questions.explanation: He is cost-focused and prefers data-heavy proposals.

questions.question: How was the 2024 annual price-reduction demand of 3% settled?

options.A: At 1.5%, linked to a new nomination

questions.explanation: Lesson: trade, don't concede.

questions.question: How much advance notice does Aravalli require for a process change (PCN)?
questions.explanation: This is a standing commitment on the account.

questions.question: What was the main lesson from the 2025 delivery slippage?

options.A: Avoid premium freight at any cost
options.B: Aravalli values early warning – tell them early, with a plan

questions.explanation: Trust was damaged mainly because the customer heard late.

day15_assessment.question: What counts as excessive absenteeism?

options.B: Two or more unexcused absences in a 30-day period

day15_assessment.explanation: Eight unexcused absences in 12 months can be grounds for termination.

day15_assessment.question: Within how many days of return must travel expense claims reach Accounts?
day15_assessment.explanation: Later claims need a reason and Function Head approval.

day15_assessment.question: What triggers an L2 escalation?

options.B: No response within 2 working days, or the customer is dissatisfied

day15_assessment.explanation: L2 goes to the function head plus KAM Head within 24 hours.

day15_assessment.question: Before giving any gift to a customer, what is required?

options.C: Compliance with the Code of Conduct and your manager's pre-approval

day15_assessment.explanation: Gifts must be nominal, non-cash and pre-authorised.

day15_assessment.question: A customer-requested engineering change (ECN) should be handled how?

options.B: Routed to Engineering for feasibility, cost and timing impact, then answered through the quotation process

day15_assessment.explanation: Changes must be formally assessed and priced.

day15_assessment.question: A customer disputes an invoice and an overdue payment. Who is the primary owner?
day15_assessment.explanation: The KAM follows up; Finance AR owns payments and credit/debit notes.

day15_assessment.question: You have a judgement question about the history of the Aravalli account. Who is the best person to ask?
day15_assessment.explanation: The mentor owns account knowledge and answers judgement questions.

day15_assessment.question: At Aravalli (demo account), who is the champion for PVNA's EV products?
day15_assessment.explanation: Chief Engineer – EV Platforms.

day15_assessment.question: Who receives whistle-blower incident reports under the vigil mechanism?
day15_assessment.explanation: Anonymity is allowed except for harassment, child labour, discrimination and human-rights cases.

day15_assessment.question: Who is the final gatekeeper who certifies Day-30 readiness for independent pricing and customer ownership?

options.C: The Reporting Boss / KAM Head, with HR and the mentor

day15_assessment.explanation: Certification is based on gates, not days elapsed.

day15_assessment.question: Which of these is part of the RFQ completeness checklist?

options.A: Annual and lifetime volumes by year

day15_assessment.explanation: Also drawings, specs, SOP date, deadline and commercial terms.

day15_assessment.question: How should an OEM's annual price-reduction (APR) demand be handled?

options.B: Negotiated in the annual price discussion, ideally traded for something in return

day15_assessment.explanation: Avoid ad-hoc concessions; trade, don't concede.

day15_assessment.question: Who approves premium freight at PVNA's cost?
day15_assessment.explanation: A certified KAM can recommend; the KAM Head approves.

day15_assessment.question: What is the internal target for RFQ response turnaround?

options.B: Within 10 working days (and always before the customer's deadline)

day15_assessment.explanation: Part of the KAM KPIs.

day15_assessment.question: Why do payment terms matter commercially?
day15_assessment.explanation: Hence CFO approval for any change.

day15_assessment.question: Which of these is a Hybrid-category product?
day15_assessment.explanation: Hybrids need vapour management because the engine runs less often.

day15_assessment.question: What is an MCU/VCU?

options.C: A Motor / Vehicle Control Unit used in EVs

day15_assessment.explanation: Listed in PVNA's EV category.

day15_assessment.question: Which sensors come from PVNA's 2008–2013 JV with TT Electronics?

options.A: Wheel-speed sensors (WSS) and accelerator pedal sensors (APS)

day15_assessment.explanation: Sensor heritage for the group.

day15_assessment.question: What was the company's first product in the 1990s?
day15_assessment.explanation: The horn business was later divested to Hella (2005).

day15_assessment.question: In which segment would you most typically discuss the Exhaust Brake Valve?
day15_assessment.explanation: Exhaust brakes are a commercial-vehicle application.
